name: Breccia Spur
geological_features: Shattered cliff faces from ancient impacts
specific_features: A massive impact scar exposing deep mantle strata
Fields of metallic debris from a destroyed companion body
description: Breccia Spur is a small, airless rocky world bearing the scars of a violent past. Its surface is a shattered landscape of impact craters, fractured cliff faces, and exposed metallic strata, suggesting the planet suffered a catastrophic collision event in its distant history.

Without atmosphere, the surface endures unfiltered radiation and extreme temperature swings between its sun-facing and shadow sides. The terrain is jagged and treacherous, with loose rubble fields and razor-edged rock formations that would challenge any ground operation.

Geological analysis indicates that Breccia Spur may once have been significantly larger, with a substantial portion of its mass ejected by a planetary-scale impact. Fields of metallic debris in the surrounding orbital space support this theory, painting a picture of ancient destruction on a staggering scale.

The exposed mantle and core fragments make Breccia Spur an unusually rich source of heavy metals, with platinum and titanium concentrations far exceeding typical rocky bodies. Mining consortiums have flagged it as a high-priority extraction site, though the unstable terrain presents significant engineering challenges.
